title: Human-environment relationships (reciprocal relationship)
competency: Examine the reciprocal relationships between humans and the environment.

keywords.def: A person. Humans need the environment for food, water, fuel and shelter.
The surroundings we live in: climate, relief, soil, water, plants and animals.
A relationship in which both sides affect each other.

ideas.name: The environment shapes how people live

en.text: Every living thing depends on its environment. People get food, water, fuel, medicines and building materials from it. Climate, relief and soil shape how people live and where they settle. Good climate, fertile soil and enough water attract many people. Very hot, cold or dry places with poor soil have few people.

screens.title: Where would you settle?
screens.ask: Where would most farmers choose to settle?
opts: A cool, rainy highland with fertile soil
screens.after: Most people settle where the climate is good, the soil is fertile and there is enough water. The environment influences where people live.

screens.title: 3.1 Human-environment relationships
paras: Every living thing on the earth depends on its environment.
Humans get food, water, fuel, medicines and building materials from it.

screens.title: The environment influences people
paras: Climate, relief, soil and the like influence peoples' mode of life.
A favorable climate, fertile soil and enough water attract many people.
Very hot, cold or dry places with infertile soil discourage large settlement.
This shows how the environment influences population distribution.
table: Favorable climate, fertile soil, enough water
Extremely hot, cold or dry climate, infertile soil, little water

screens.title: Elements of the physical environment
screens.ask: Tap each element to see how it shapes life.
items: Rain and temperature decide which crops grow and how people dress and build.
Highlands, lowlands and slopes affect farming and travel.
Fertile soil feeds many people; poor soil feeds few.
Rivers, lakes and springs attract settlement.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The surroundings we live in: climate, relief, soil, water, plants and animals.
A person. Humans need the environment for food, water, fuel and shelter.

screens.text: Which conditions attract a large population?
opts: Favorable climate, fertile soil and enough water
screens.ans: Favorable climate, fertile soil and enough water
screens.why: The book says these positively influence population concentration.
screens.clue: Which conditions make farming and living easy?

screens.text: Areas with infertile soil and inadequate water discourage large human settlement.
screens.why: The book says unfavorable climate, infertile soil and little water discourage settlement.
screens.clue: Would many people live where crops cannot grow?

screens.text: Which things do humans get from the environment? Tap all.
screens.why: The book lists all five: food, water, fuel, medicines and building materials.
screens.clue: Think of what you eat, drink, burn and build with.

screens.text: Why do few people live in the Danakil Depression?
opts: It is extremely hot and dry, with little water
It has too much fertile soil
It is too cold and rainy
screens.ans: It is extremely hot and dry, with little water
screens.why: The Danakil is one of the hottest places on earth and has little fresh water. Unfavorable climate and little water discourage settlement.
screens.clue: Use the book's list of conditions that discourage settlement.

en.text: The environment always affects people. But people can also change their environment with their skill, knowledge and experience. Technology helps them make suitable places to live. So the relationship is reciprocal: both affect each other.

screens.title: Hot weather and food
screens.ask: In hot places food spoils fast. What have people done about it since ancient times?
screens.after: People used their skill and knowledge: drying, smoking, salting and fermenting food. They changed how they live to fit the environment.

screens.title: People influence the environment
paras: The influence of environment on humans' activity is unavoidable.
But people can modify their environment with skill, knowledge and experience.
Advancing technology helps humans create conducive environments.

screens.title: A two-way bond
paras: There is an inseparable bond between human beings and nature.
The relationship between the two is highly reciprocal: both affect each other.

screens.title: Which way does it go?
items: People bring water to new places.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A relationship in which both sides affect each other.

screens.text: What does "reciprocal relationship" between humans and the environment mean?
screens.why: The book says the relationship is highly reciprocal (both affect each other).

screens.text: People can modify their environment with their skill, knowledge and experience.
screens.why: The book says so; technology helps them create conducive environments.

screens.text: Which is an example of people modifying the environment?
opts: Building irrigation canals to water dry land
screens.ans: Building irrigation canals to water dry land
screens.why: Canals are made by people using skill and technology. Rain and floods are natural.

screens.text: A family in Afar keeps meat by drying it in the sun. Which statement explains this best?
opts: The hot climate spoils food, so people use skill to preserve it
The environment has no effect on food
People in hot places never preserve food
screens.ans: The hot climate spoils food, so people use skill to preserve it
screens.why: The environment (heat) affects people, and people respond with skill and knowledge. Both sides act: a reciprocal relationship.
screens.clue: Find the cause from the environment and the human response.

items.text: What influences humans to practise different food preservation methods?
opts: The environment, such as high temperature that spoils food
items.ans: The environment, such as high temperature that spoils food
items.why: High temperature makes food perish easily, so people preserve it.
items.clue: Why does food spoil quickly in some areas?

items.text: It is possible for humans to modify their environment with the help of their skill, knowledge and experience.
items.why: People use skill, knowledge, experience and technology to change their surroundings.

items.text: "The relationship between human and the environment is reciprocal." What does this mean?
opts: The environment influences people, and people modify the environment
items.ans: The environment influences people, and people modify the environment
items.why: Reciprocal means both affect each other.

items.text: Which are traditional food preservation methods? Tap all.
items.why: Drying, salting and smoking are old methods. A refrigerator is a modern method.

test.text: Which of these is NOT something humans get from the environment?
test.why: Food, fuel and medicines come from the environment.

test.text: The relationship between humans and the environment is reciprocal.
Which area discourages large human settlement?
opts: An area with extremely dry climate and infertile soil
An area with fertile soil and enough water
test.ans: An area with extremely dry climate and infertile soil
test.why: Unfavorable climate and infertile soil discourage settlement.

test.ask: People modify their environment with their skill, knowledge and ___.
test.why: The book says skill, knowledge and experience.

test.text: Terracing a steep slope so crops can grow is an example of:
test.why: People use skill to change the land to suit their needs.

notes.text: Activity 3.1 Q1 (food preservation in your locality) is open; it is asked as a pick of traditional methods (model answer, not from the book).
The Danakil and Afar examples in challenges are added Ethiopian context.
